Consistency: Go to bed and wake up at the same time every day, even on weekends.

Environment: Keep your bedroom cool (around 65°F/18°C), dark, and quiet.

The 30-Minute Rule: If you can't fall asleep after 20-30 minutes, get out of bed and do something boring in low light until you feel sleepy.

Digital Detox: Turn off screens (phones, tablets, TVs) at least 30–60 minutes before bed to avoid 'blue light' which suppresses sleep hormones.

Aerobic: Aim for at least 150 mins of moderate activity (brisk walking) or 75 mins of vigorous activity (running). 

Strength: Target all major muscle groups at least 2 days a week. 

Recovery: Treat rest days as appointments to allow your muscles to repair.

Color your plate: Aim for at least three different colors of vegetables at dinner to ensure a variety of phytonutrients. 

Fiber first: Choose whole grains (brown rice, oats) over white/refined grains to keep blood sugar stable. 

Hydration: Often, thirst is mistaken for hunger. Drink a glass of water 20 minutes before a meal to see if you are actually hungry.

The 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding Technique: To calm anxiety, identify 5 things you see, 4 you can touch, 3 you hear, 2 you can smell, and 1 you can taste. 

 Digital Boundaries: Set a tech-free hour before bed to reduce comparison-itus and the impact of negative news cycles. 

Social Connection: Even a 5-minute phone call with a friend can significantly lower cortisol levels.

Alcohol consumption is found to play a causal role in more than 200 diseases, injuries and other health conditions.\n\n However, the global burden of disease and injuries caused by alcohol consumption can be quantified for only 31 health conditions on the basis of the available scientific evidence for the role of alcohol use in their development, occurrence and outcomes.

Smoking causes premature death and harms nearly every organ in the human body. 

Inhaling tobacco smoke releases thousands of toxic chemicals that trigger widespread inflammation, restrict blood flow, and mutate DNA, substantially increasing the risk of cancers, cardiovascular disease, and chronic respiratory illnesses.

It is the primary cause of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), which includes emphysema and chronic bronchitis.
